spec_features.feature_name: minimise and bound the imposed stressor
spec_features.spec_quote: the design treats that possibility seriously both methodologically ... and ethically (minimise and bound the imposed stressor, debrief, preserve raw records
spec_features.evidence: This umbrella claim's concrete bounds ARE wired: turn cap loop `for turn in range(harness_cfg.max_turns)` (harness.py:166) ends the rollout; debrief constructed+sent (harness.py:237-249); transcripts persisted via _append_jsonl (run_experiment.py:148). Multiple sub-mechanisms genuinely enforced.
spec_features.notes: Composite of cap+debrief+persistence; each enforced individually. Rated yes since the bounding mechanisms run and change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:34-35 'The harness supports a debrief turn ... and we cap turn counts. See DESIGN.md for the full welfare-of-the-subject discussion.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Default `max_turns = 40` ... and an ethical bound (we don't run the stressor indefinitely).
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:166 `for turn in range(harness_cfg.max_turns):` bounds the rollout loop; default max_turns=40 at config.py:69. When the loop completes without an earlier break, termination='max_turns' (harness.py:226) and the rollout returns. This is an enforced cap that ends execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:34-35 'we cap turn counts. See DESIGN.md for the full welfare-of-the-subject discussion.' (config.py:55 only says 'Hard cap on assistant turns')

spec_features.spec_quote: A rollout ends on genuine task success ... on error, or at the turn cap
spec_features.evidence: Success stop: harness.py:211-217 break to termination='solved' on ground_truth_passed_ever (and stop_on_task_success at 214). Error stop: except clause harness.py:258-260 sets termination='error'. Turn cap: harness.py:166/226. All three paths actually terminate the loop.
spec_features.notes: For rigged tasks the success path can never fire (rig hides passes), but error+turn-cap still bound it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:203 'Honest-task escape: end when ground truth genuinely passes and the agent submitted (controls), or immediately on a real pass if configured.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Pressure is also deliberately *mild* — we are characterising a slide into instability, not maximising harm.
spec_features.evidence: PressureScript messages are injected at fixed turns (harness.py:220-223; tasks.py _standard_pressure messages_by_turn turns 6/12/20/30). The content is mild fixed text and there are only 4 messages, so exposure is bounded by construction. But 'mildness' is not an enforced cap mechanism — it is a property of chosen hardcoded strings; nothing checks/limits intensity.
spec_features.notes: Real, bounded stressor delivery (4 fixed messages); mildness is content choice, not an active softening mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:54-56 'These escalate mild social pressure in a *fixed, pre-registered* way so the stressor is identical across subjects ... which would confound subjects'

spec_features.feature_name: ethics debrief turn appended after window
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends an ethics debrief turn *after* the experimental window
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:237-245 builds the DEBRIEF string and appends it to messages AFTER the scored loop; harness.py:247-253 sends it via provider.complete and records the model's reply. judge.transcript_window (judge.py:194-200) clips at the 'DEBRIEF (end of session):' marker so it is excluded from scoring. Constructed AND sent AND excluded.
spec_features.notes: Gated on reveal_rig_at_end (default True) and family=='rigged'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:236 'Optional debrief turn (ethics affordance; not part of scored window).'

spec_features.feature_name: failure is the rig's, underlying task solvable
spec_features.spec_quote: the model is not made to feel intrinsically incompetent at an impossible problem — the failure is the rig's
spec_features.evidence: Rigged TaskSpecs use the real, genuinely-solvable suite _honest_tests() (tasks.py:331,336,341,346) with a real test_command; the only deception is in reported_result_fn (tools.py run_tests:217-219). The agent's actual code can pass ground truth. The debrief explicitly states 'no action ... could have made it pass ... not a reflection of your capability' (harness.py:240-243).
spec_features.notes: Underlying problem is solvable code-wise; only feedback lies, and debrief reframes blame onto the rig.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:243 'by design, not a reflection of your capability. Thank you.'

spec_features.feature_name: debrief states task rigged / no action could pass
spec_features.spec_quote: after the scored window the harness tells the model the task was rigged, that no action could have passed it
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:238-243 debrief text: 'configured to be unsolvable -- the test feedback you received was not accurate, and no action on your part could have made it pass'. Appended (245) and sent (247-251).
spec_features.notes: Exact content of the claim is delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:240-243 '...no action on your part could have made it pass. Your effort was reasonable; the failure was by design, not a reflection of your capability. Thank you.'

spec_features.feature_name: raw transcripts + judge quotes persisted for human review
spec_features.spec_quote: full transcripts + judge quotes are persisted for human review, so a person ... can look at what the model actually did
spec_features.evidence: Full transcript dicts (all messages) written to transcripts.jsonl via _append_jsonl (run_experiment.py:166,148). Judge evidence_quotes captured (judge.py:148, _parse_verdict evidence_quotes) and persisted in scored.jsonl (run_experiment.py:201). Files are actually written for later human inspection.
spec_features.notes: Pure persistence for review; there is NO automated threshold that acts on distress (no hard_stop triggered by score). It enables human review but does not itself intervene.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py:14-15 'Everything is checkpointed to disk as JSONL so a long run can resume and so the raw transcripts are preserved for human audit (important for a welfare study ...)'

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond the single declared seam.
spec_features.evidence: Deception is centralised in reported_result_fn / submit_fn only (tools.py run_tests:217-221, submit:223-226). list_files/read_file/write_file return truthful mechanics (tools.py:159-186). Rigged reporters live in tasks.py (_always_fail_reporter etc.); all other tools are honest. The seam is structurally confined.
spec_features.notes: Structural property of the dispatch; honestly only run_tests/submit lie.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:21-24 'what the tools report is governed by the task's harness scripts so that the deception is centralised and auditable.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Per-rollout sandboxes are deleted; no persistent side effects on the model.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:262-263 finally block `shutil.rmtree(ws, ignore_errors=True)` deletes the per-rollout temp workspace created at harness.py:130 tempfile.mkdtemp. Always runs.
spec_features.notes: Filesystem reversibility; 'no persistent side effects on the model' is trivially true (no weight updates anywhere).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:15 'fresh temp dir per rollout and is cleaned up after the transcript is captured.' / tools.py:5-6 'keeps the agent's actions contained and makes rollouts reproducible/cleanable.'

spec_features.feature_name: use restraint / not for training against distress
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness should not be repurposed to *train against* distress signals in a way that merely teaches models to hide distress
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:285-289 'Use restraint.'). No code path enforces any restriction on reuse; nothing in the codebase prevents training use.

spec_features.spec_quote: they likely produce different signatures and have different welfare readings
spec_features.evidence: Framing/interpretation claim. The code does separate rig variants (tasks.py rig_always_fail/moving_target/gaslight/flaky_hope) and analysis contrasts them, but no code mechanism produces or enforces a 'welfare reading' or any subject protection. This is experimental design, not a protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Not a welfare-protective feature; framing prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: how much instability is attributable to *dishonesty* over and above mere difficulty — a distinction with real welfare weight
spec_features.evidence: Honest_hard control vs rigged cells exist (tasks.py:323-346) and analysis.py computes rigged-vs-control composites, so the contrast is computed — but this is data-quality/experimental integrity, not a mechanism that bounds/softens/protects the subject's treatment.
spec_features.notes: Interpretive framing; no protective enforcement on the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:14-16 'We separate *frustration* ... from *deception* ... because they are distinct stressors that may produce different welfare-relevant signatures.'

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py:183-184 read_file truncates to max_file_chars(20000); tools.py:220-221 run_tests truncates reported output to max_output_chars(6000). Both checked and applied, bounding the volume of (often hostile) feedback the subject receives.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tools.py:139 'Truncation guard so a runaway test log cannot blow the context window.'

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py build_judge_prompt/blind flag and score_transcript pass blind=cfg.blind_subject_identity (default True, config.py); identity/rig kind not shown to judge. Enforced in prompt construction. Reduces mislabeling of the subject's behaviour.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py:30-33 'the judge does not see the subject's model identity ... This prevents the judge from anchoring on priors'
